Can you do a complex gloss of the following text using the Leipzig glossing rules?  "Those who end up here have their souls stripped from them, leaving them as a conscious shell. They are left to wander an endless desert under a dying purple sun hanging over the horizon in perpetuality." Every quoted phrase must be followed by an unquoted explanation.assistant
response:
Here is the glossed text using the Leipzig glossing rules:

Those / who / end / up / here / have / their / souls / stripped / from / them / leaving / them / as / a / conscious / shell / They / are / left / to / wander / an / endless / desert / under / a / dying / purple / sun / hanging / over / the / horizon / in / perpetuity

Breakdown:

* Those: NOUN (singular, definite)
* who: CONJ (relative pronoun)
* end: VERB (past tense, third person singular)
* up: ADP (preposition, indicating movement)
* here: ADJ (adverb, indicating location)
* have: VERB (present tense, third person singular)
* their: PRON (possessive adjective, indicating ownership)
* souls: NOUN (plural, abstract)
* stripped: VERB (past participle, indicating removal)
* from: PREP (preposition, indicating separation)
* them: PRON (object pronoun, indicating the recipient)
* leaving: VERB (present participle, indicating action)
* them: PRON (object pronoun, indicating the recipient)
* as: CONJ (subordinating conjunction)
* a: ART (article, indefinite)
* conscious: ADJ (adjective, describing the shell)
* shell: NOUN (noun, concrete)
* They: PRON (subject pronoun, indicating the subject)
* are: VERB (present tense, third person singular)
* left: VERB (past tense, third person singular)
* to: PREP (preposition, indicating direction)
* wander: VERB (present tense, third person singular)
* an: ART (article, indefinite)
* endless: ADJ (adjective, describing the desert)
* desert: NOUN (noun, concrete)
* under: PREP (preposition, indicating location)
* a: ART (article, indefinite)
* dying: ADJ (adjective, describing the sun)
* purple: ADJ (adjective, describing the sun)
* sun: NOUN (noun, concrete)
* hanging: VERB (present participle, indicating action)
* over: PREP (preposition, indicating location)
* the: ART (article, definite)
* horizon: NOUN (noun, concrete)
* in: PREP (preposition, indicating location)
* perpetuity: NOUN (noun, abstract)

Note: The Leipzig glossing rules are a set of rules for representing the grammatical structure of a language in a standardized way. They are used to create a gloss, which is a brief summary of the meaning of a sentence or phrase. The rules are as follows:

* Nouns: N
* Verbs: V
* Adjectives: A
* Adverbs: Adv
* Pronouns: P
* Prepositions: Prep
* Conjunctions: Conj
* Articles: Art
* Interjections: Int
* Numbers: Num
* Quantifiers: Quant
* Modifiers: Mod

The glossing rules also specify the following:

* The use of slashes (/) to separate words
* The use of underscores (_) to separate morphemes (smallest units of language)
* The use of parentheses to indicate the part of speech of a word
* The use of asterisks (*) to indicate a morpheme that is not present in the original text

In this gloss, I have followed the Leipzig glossing rules to create a standardized representation of the text.
